LANTERNS IN TWO LONG SAGS: paper lanterns strung in two long sags between the upper balconies of both banks, the lower line hanging right down toward the water and the upper one crossing higher, a few lanterns missing from the middle of the lower string, the wall faces between the stalls carrying stacked crates and a coil of rope hung on a peg

LANTERNS AT THREE HEIGHTS: three lines of paper lanterns crossing between opposite balconies at three clearly different heights, the lowest sagging deepest and carrying rounder lanterns, the topmost line shorter and strung tight against the eaves at one end only, the wall faces between the stalls thick with a climbing vine gone right up to the eaves

LANTERNS UNEVEN AND DENSE: a dense run of paper lanterns strung between brackets on the far bank and a jutting balcony corner on the near side, the line bowing unevenly so most lanterns cluster toward the heavier end, one hanging at a sharp angle, the wall faces between the stalls lined with potted plants on brackets at uneven heights

LANTERNS OFF TO ONE SIDE: a long sag of paper lanterns anchored high on a corner bracket and drooping down to a low balcony rail far to one side of the frame, a second shorter string crossing behind it at a different angle, the two lines crossing at clearly different angles, the wall faces between the stalls carrying a row of shuttered windows with their shutters thrown back

BALCONIES ALMOST TOUCHING: two balconies leaning out over the canal from opposite banks until only a narrow gap remains between them, one rail crowded with potted plants spilling stems over the edge, the other carrying a single bright chair pushed into the far corner, the wall faces between the stalls hung with drying bundles and one small brazier burning low

BALCONY WITH BIRDCAGE AND CLOTH: a wide timber balcony cantilevered out over the water with a birdcage hung from its corner post, a damp cloth draped over the rail to one side, and three mismatched clay pots of different heights standing along the sill, the wall faces between the stalls stacked with baskets to shoulder height and a leaning broom

BALCONY DENSE WITH PLANTS: a pair of balconies at different heights on the same bank, both with plants spilling thick off every rail, one carrying a tall climbing stem trained up a bamboo pole lashed to the wall, the upper balcony narrower and set slightly further back, the wall faces between the stalls bare warm stone with one wooden bench and a heap of nets beside it

BALCONY CORNER WITH AWNING: a corner balcony jutting out at an angle with a striped cloth awning stretched on thin bamboo poles above it, several large leafed plants drooping over the rail on the left side only, a stool visible through the open shutter behind, the wall faces between the stalls hung with big glazed water jars on iron hooks

THE STACKED CROSSINGS: a high stone arch entering from one side edge of the frame and running back out of it so only its near flank and the top of its crown show, a smaller timber footbridge cropped by the same edge lower down behind them both, a small tiled tea-house built onto the middle of the timber bridge, the wall faces between the stalls carrying a rough timber stair going up and a cat-sized hole cut low in one

BRIDGE ARCH CROPPING THE EDGE: a wide stone bridge arch entering from the right edge of the frame so only one flank and the crown are visible, the town roofline stepping up behind it, a small sprite figure paused side-on at the highest point of the visible span, the wall faces between the stalls draped with hanks of dyed yarn in five colours

TWO BRIDGES DIFFERENT HEIGHTS: a high narrow stone arch entering from one side edge of the frame high up with its far end out of shot, and a lower wider timber bridge cropped by the same edge nearer the water, crossing at a different angle below it, the two at plainly different heights with a gap of clear space between, the wall faces between the stalls carrying stacked crates and a coil of rope hung on a peg

BRIDGE WITH TEA-HOUSE: a timber bridge entering from one side edge of the frame with its far end out of shot and a small tiled structure built onto the part that shows, the structure's roof slightly taller on one side, a rope tied to its corner post hanging slack down toward the water, the wall faces between the stalls thick with a climbing vine gone right up to the eaves

LAUNDRY IN FLAT BLOCKS: laundry strung in flat bright blocks of colour between upper windows across a wide gap, the pieces at uneven intervals and different widths, a pulley basket hanging from one of the lines and resting partway down toward the water below, the wall faces between the stalls lined with potted plants on brackets at uneven heights

LAUNDRY AND PULLEY LINE: three lines of laundry crossing between the upper storeys of both banks at different heights, the lowest carrying heavier dark cloth, a pulley rope running alongside the rightmost line with a small basket stopped at an angle mid-descent, the wall faces between the stalls carrying a row of shuttered windows with their shutters thrown back

LAUNDRY WITH ONE ODD PIECE: a long run of laundry between two upper windows, most pieces flat and evenly coloured but one large piece bunched and knotted around its line, a second shorter line angled below it carrying only two items far apart from each other, the wall faces between the stalls hung with drying bundles and one small brazier burning low

ROOFLINES STEPPING UP: rooflines stepping up and down in uneven jumps across the far bank, one tiled turret standing clearly taller than everything around it with a small rounded hat perched on its chimney, a dovecote sitting low on the nearest ridge to one side, the wall faces between the stalls stacked with baskets to shoulder height and a leaning broom

TURRET AND DOVECOTE: a tiled turret rising above the surrounding roofline at the left of the frame with its chimney cap slightly off-centre, a small dovecote on a lower ridge further right, the roofline between them dipping then rising again in two unequal steps, the wall faces between the stalls bare warm stone with one wooden bench and a heap of nets beside it

ROOFLINES IN THREE LEVELS: rooflines across the far bank arranged in three distinct levels, the tallest section far to one side, a wide low section in the middle dropping sharply, and a narrow stepped section at the far end with a single chimney standing apart from the rest, the wall faces between the stalls hung with big glazed water jars on iron hooks

THE GREAT WATERWHEEL: a great wooden waterwheel turning against a tiled wall with chunky stepped pixel spray caught around its lower paddles, a timber chute fixed to the wall beside it pouring a bright flat trickle of water down in hard pixel steps into the canal, the wall faces between the stalls carrying a rough timber stair going up and a cat-sized hole cut low in one

WATERWHEEL WITH CHUTE: a wide wooden waterwheel set against a tiled wall at an angle to the frame, its paddles built in three uneven widths, a wooden chute running from a window opening above it and pouring a blocky flat stream of water down across the wheel's upper rim, the wall faces between the stalls draped with hanks of dyed yarn in five colours

WHEEL AND UPPER GEAR: a wooden waterwheel turning at the base of a tall tiled wall, a second smaller wooden wheel mounted higher on the same wall connected to the first by a thick rope wrapped in blocky pixel steps, a timber chute below the upper wheel trickling water into the canal, the wall faces between the stalls carrying stacked crates and a coil of rope hung on a peg

TIMBER GALLERY WITH FIGURES: a timber gallery running the full length of the far bank one storey above the water, three small sprite figures side-on along it each busy with a different task, a steep stair descending from the gallery's far end down toward the canal surface, the wall faces between the stalls thick with a climbing vine gone right up to the eaves

UPPER WALKWAY AND STAIR: a narrow timber walkway running along the upper storey of one bank with uneven post spacing, two small sprite figures at different points along it both facing away, a stair dropping from its nearer end at an angle with a coil of rope hung on the lowest post, the wall faces between the stalls lined with potted plants on brackets at uneven heights

BOAT HOISTED UNDER EAVES: a small boat hauled up on two ropes under the deep eaves of an upper storey, its hull at a slight angle so the bow hangs lower than the stern, the ropes tied off to a thick bracket fixed into the wall planking above, the wall faces between the stalls carrying a row of shuttered windows with their shutters thrown back

CRATES ON A FLAT ROOF: a flat upper roof beside a wide chimney stack carrying a stack of plain crates in three unequal piles, a coil of rope resting against the tallest pile, a single timber pole leaning across the corner of the roof at an angle, the wall faces between the stalls hung with drying bundles and one small brazier burning low
